prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right choice depends on your exact location in Atlanta, budget, timeline, the size/age of your home, and whether you want a high‑efficiency system or a basic replacement. I can help you pick the best contractor for your situation. First, a few quick questions:

- What Atlanta zip code/neighborhood are you in?
- Is this for a single-family home, condo, or multi‑unit property?
- Roughly what size is the house (sq ft) and how many tons / age of the existing system (if known)?
- Any brand or efficiency (SEER) preference?
- Do you need financing or want to use a specific rebate/utility program?
- How soon do you want the replacement done?

While you answer, here’s a short, practical checklist and selection process you can use right away:

What to require from any installer
- Written, itemized estimate (equipment, labor, refrigerant line costs, permits, thermostat) — get at least 3 bids.
- Load calculation (Manual J) and duct assessment (Manual D or duct leakage check) — don’t accept a “rule of thumb” sizing.
- Specify make/model and SEER rating; compare apples-to-apples.
- Ask about NATE-certified technicians, ACCA membership, and years in business.
- Verify license and insurance (general liability + workers’ comp).
- Ask about equipment warranty and installation warranty (labor).
- Confirm who pulls permits and handles local code inspections.
- Request references or recent local reviews; check Google, BBB, Angi/HomeAdvisor.
- Get a clear timeline and payment schedule; avoid large upfront payments.

Questions to ask each contractor
- Will you perform a Manual J and ductwork inspection?
- What exact unit (brand/model) are you quoting and what’s included?
- Is existing ductwork adequate or will repairs be needed?
- What warranty on labor and parts? Is it transferable?
- Do you provide maintenance plans?
- What happens if additional issues are found mid-job?

Red flags
- Extremely low bids with vague scopes.
- No written contract or unclear exclusions.
- No local references or poor review patterns.
- Sales pressure to sign immediately.

If you want, provide your zip code and preferences and I’ll give a short list of highly rated Atlanta-area companies and specific questions tailored to those options (I can’t book for you, but I’ll prepare the shortlist and comparison points).
